source_caption:
Law Abiding Citizen — Justice Has a Price

Law Abiding Citizen (2009) follows Clyde Shelton, a family man whose life is destroyed when his wife and daughter are brutally murdered during a home invasion. When the justice system fails to deliver the punishment he believes the killers deserve, Clyde becomes consumed by anger and betrayal.

Years later, Clyde begins carrying out a carefully planned campaign against the people he believes allowed the system to fail his family. Prosecutor Nick Rice finds himself at the center of the conflict, forced to confront an opponent who appears to have anticipated every move.

As the situation escalates, Clyde's actions challenge the boundaries between justice and revenge. His plans become increasingly elaborate, forcing authorities to question how far someone can go when they believe the system has failed them.

The film explores themes of justice, revenge, corruption, morality, and the consequences of taking the law into your own hands. It raises difficult questions about whether justice can truly be achieved outside the system.

What makes Law Abiding Citizen compelling is the psychological battle between Clyde and Nick, with each trying to stay one step ahead as the stakes continue to rise.

💬 When the system fails you, how far would you go to make things right?

source_details.synopsis: Law Abiding Citizen is a 2009 American vigilante action thriller film directed by F. Gary Gray and written by Kurt Wimmer. The film stars Jamie Foxx, Gerard Butler, Bruce McGill, Colm Meaney, Leslie Bibb, Regina Hall, Michael Irby, Christian Stolte, and Josh Stewart. Set in Philadelphia, it follows Clyde Shelton (Butler), a man who witnesses the rape and murder of his wife and daughter during a home invasion.
